title: The spice trade of the Moluccas
summary: The search for direct access to the lucrative Eastern spice trade was a major motive of the European Age of Exploration. The Banda Islands were the original and sole source of nutmeg and mace during the most prosperous years of colonization. Francisco Serrão sailed to the Spice Islands in 1512, the Dutch challenged the Portuguese from 1596, and in the 17th century built a nutmeg plantation system to hold a monopoly.

uncertainty.note: Inter-island trade in cloves and nutmeg existed earlier, but the Moluccan sultanates and long-distance maritime export network expanded rapidly around 1300; European powers intervened from 1500 onwards, culminating in the Dutch East India Company monopoly in the 17th century.

as_recorded.value: In the 15th century, spices came to Europe

where.modern_name: Banda Islands and northern Maluku, Indonesia
where.historical_name: Maluku Islands (Banda Islands for nutmeg and mace; Ternate and Tidore for cloves)

importance.justification: The botanical monopoly on cloves and nutmeg in the Moluccas drove global maritime trade routes, motivated European voyages of exploration, and led to colonial monopolies.

sources.title: The Spice Trade & the Age of Exploration
sources.author: Mark Cartwright

reviewer_note: The start date is approximate and marks the European-era trade, though Asian trade in these spices is older. The source for Banda is a UNESCO tentative listing written by Indonesia.
